newsitem.title: USA: N.Y. Times in pact with Newspaper Guild.
newsitem.headline: N.Y. Times in pact with Newspaper Guild.

text.p: The New York Times said Friday it reached a tentative agreement on a labor contract extension through 2003 that includes a two percent annual salary increase beginning 1997.
The agreement was reached after extensive negotiations with the the guild, which represents clerical, business, news and editorial employees of the newspaper, the Times said.
The contract is subject to ratification by the Newspaper Guild's 1,500 members at the Times and a ratification meeting is planned for September, the newspaper said.

The contract includes a one-time, three percent bonus for 1996 and a ban on all layoffs for the entire term of the extended agreement for regular fulll-time and part-time employees currently on the Times' payroll, it said.
Arthur Sulzberger Jr., publisher of The Times, said the newspaper was delighted to have reached this agreement.
"Now we can turn all of our attention to the exciting launch next month of The Times's new six-section, color daily newspaper for the next generation of readers and advertisers," he said.
Barry Lipton, president of the guild, said the contract was "a superior agreement", which addresses the concerns of the guild's members.
The Newspaper Guild of New York represents 3,700 workers at more than 20 media organizations in the metropolitan area.
